verdict.summary: You can create a Google Cloud OAuth client and connect your own Gmail account in minutes. Going public is hard. Sensitive scopes like gmail.send need Google verification, which Google says takes 3-5 business days. Full mail access (https://mail.google.com/, which is in Composio's default scopes) is restricted: verification can take several weeks, and if Gmail data reaches your servers you also need a CASA security assessment every year.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for the client and testing; 1-3 days to prepare verification materials; more for a CASA assessment if you use restricted scopes
verdict.approval_wait: Sensitive scopes: 3-5 business days per Google, but 2026 forum posts report 1-2+ months. Restricted scopes: several weeks or more, plus a CASA assessment

gates.name: Testing (unverified app, your own account)
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own Google account through your own OAuth client and call the Gmail API through Composio.
limits: Unverified-app warning screen appears before consent
Refresh tokens expire after 7 days while the app is in Testing, unless you request only basic name, email and profile scopes

gates.name: Testing / unverified with invited users
gates.unlocks: A limited group of other users can connect while the app is unverified.
limits: Unverified apps that request sensitive or restricted scopes are capped at 100 new users. Using up the cap can disable sign-in for new users
Users see the unverified-app warning screen
Refresh tokens expire after 7 days in Testing status, so users must reconnect weekly
A third-party guide says personal @gmail.com accounts always count toward the 100-user cap, but allowlisted Workspace accounts do not (unofficial)

gates.name: In production and verified (brand + sensitive/restricted scope verification)
gates.unlocks: Anyone can connect, with no 100-user cap and no warning screen.
limits: Restricted scopes need reverification and a new security assessment at least every 12 months
Brand verification must be done first. A compliant result expires after 7 days if you don't publish
gates.time_to_reach: Sensitive only: 3-5 business days officially; community posts report 1-2+ months. Restricted: several weeks or more, plus CASA assessment time

steps.title: Sign in to Google Cloud and create a project
steps.detail: Sign in at the Google Cloud console with the Google account that will own the app. Create a new project for this integration. The OAuth client, consent screen and verification record all belong to this project.
gotchas: Use an account and email inboxes you will keep watching. Google's Trust & Safety team contacts the project's email addresses during review.

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API in the project
steps.detail: Go to APIs & Services, open the API Library, find the Gmail API and enable it for this project. If you keep Composio's default scopes, also enable the People API.

steps.title: Choose the narrowest Gmail scopes
steps.detail: List the Gmail actions your agent actually uses and match each one to the narrowest scope. For example, use gmail.send (sensitive) for send-only. Request https://mail.google.com/ (restricted) only if you truly need full access. Restricted scopes add weeks of review and a CASA assessment every year. Composio's default list also includes contacts and profile scopes; drop any you don't need.
gotchas: IMAP/SMTP access requires https://mail.google.com/ and therefore restricted-scope verification.

steps.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen and branding
steps.detail: Set the user type to External and the publishing status to Testing. Enter the app name and a support email, plus a homepage URL and privacy policy URL on a domain you own. Add that domain, and the domains of your redirect URIs, to Authorized domains. Add the scopes you chose.
gotchas: The homepage must be public (not behind a login) and cannot be a Play Store or Facebook page.
The privacy policy must be on the same domain as the homepage.

steps.title: Create a Web application OAuth client
steps.detail: In APIs & Services > Credentials, click + Create Credentials, choose OAuth client ID and set the application type to Web application. Under Authorized redirect URIs, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. Copy the Client ID and Client secret.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect URI must match exactly, or Google returns redirect_uri_mismatch.

steps.title: Add the credentials to Composio and test the authorization
steps.detail: Create a Composio auth config for the gmail toolkit using your own Client ID, Client secret and scope list. Then connect your own Google account. Google's endpoints are https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth and https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token. You will see the unverified-app warning; continue past it.
gotchas: invalid_client means the client ID is wrong or belongs to a different project.
In Testing status, refresh tokens expire after 7 days, so expect to reconnect weekly.

steps.title: Invite test users
steps.detail: Add the Google accounts of the people who will test the app to the consent screen's test-user list, then have them connect through Composio. Keep track of how many people have connected: unverified apps with sensitive or restricted scopes stop accepting new users after 100.
gotchas: A third-party guide says personal @gmail.com accounts always count toward the cap (unofficial).

steps.title: Draft the privacy policy and scope justifications
steps.detail: Draft or update the privacy policy so it says how the app accesses, uses, stores and shares Google user data. For each sensitive or restricted scope, write a justification that explains why a narrower scope would not work.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Record a video that shows the consent flow and how the app uses each requested scope. Upload it somewhere a reviewer can open it, such as an unlisted YouTube video.
gotchas: The required video contents beyond 'video demonstration' were not confirmed from an official page.

steps.title: Publish the app and submit for brand and scope verification
steps.detail: On the consent screen, click Publish App to move from Testing to Production. Then submit brand verification and data-access (scope) verification in the Verification Center, attaching your justifications and video. Automated brand checks finish in minutes; manual brand review takes 2-3 business days.
gotchas: A compliant brand-verification result expires after 7 days if you don't publish.
If you changed branding, brand verification must be finished before restricted-scope verification.

steps.title: Wait for Google review and answer Trust & Safety emails
steps.detail: Google says sensitive-scope review typically takes 3-5 business days and restricted-scope review can take several weeks. Watch the project's contact inboxes and reply quickly to Trust & Safety follow-ups. 2026 forum threads report reviews pending for more than a month with no contact.
steps.est_time: 3-5 business days to several weeks (longer reported)

steps.title: Complete a CASA security assessment (restricted scopes only)
steps.detail: If you request https://mail.google.com/ or another restricted scope and Gmail data is stored on or passes through your servers, you need a security assessment by a Google-approved assessor under the App Defense Alliance CASA framework. Sensitive-only apps (for example, gmail.send) do not need one.

steps.title: Plan for annual reverification
steps.detail: Apps with restricted scopes must be reverified and pass a new security assessment at least every 12 months after the assessor's Letter of Assessment date. Set a reminder well before that date.

requirements.item: Google account signed in to Google Cloud console, with a project
requirements.detail: You must sign in before you can create an OAuth client.

requirements.item: Exact redirect URI registered on the OAuth client
requirements.detail: Must exactly match Composio's callback URL.

requirements.item: Public homepage on a domain you own
requirements.detail: Not behind a login, clearly about the app, and not a Play Store or Facebook listing.

requirements.item: Privacy policy on the same domain as the homepage
requirements.detail: Linked from the consent screen. Must say how Google user data is accessed, used, stored or shared.
Must include the domains of the homepage, privacy policy and redirect URIs.
A justification for each scope explaining why a narrower one won't work, plus a video demonstration.

requirements.item: CASA security assessment (restricted scopes with server-side data)
requirements.detail: Done by a Google-approved assessor and repeated every 12 months.

scopes.effect: Needs restricted-scope verification (several weeks). If data is stored on or passes through servers, also needs a CASA assessment every year. Required for IMAP/SMTP. Included in Composio's defaults.
Needs sensitive-scope verification (officially 3-5 business days) but no security assessment.
If you request only basic name, email and profile scopes, Testing-mode refresh tokens don't expire after 7 days.

scopes.scope: contacts.readonly, contacts.other.readonly, user.*.read (People API scopes in Composio defaults)
scopes.effect: Their tier was not checked. Drop them if your agent doesn't need contacts or profile details, to keep verification simpler.

blockers.cause: The redirect URI sent doesn't exactly match one registered on the OAuth client.
blockers.fix: Paste Composio's exact callback URL into Authorized redirect URIs on the client.

blockers.symptom: invalid_client: The OAuth client was not found
blockers.cause: Wrong or mistyped client ID, or one from a different project.
blockers.fix: Copy the Client ID again from Credentials in the correct project into the Composio auth config.

blockers.symptom: Users have to reconnect about every 7 days
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens expire after 7 days while an External app is in Testing status with non-basic scopes.
blockers.fix: Publish the app to Production and complete verification.

blockers.symptom: New users can't sign in; the app hit the user cap
blockers.cause: Unverified apps with sensitive or restricted scopes are capped at 100 new users.
blockers.fix: Complete verification. Until then, be selective about who you invite.

blockers.symptom: Verification stuck 'under review' for weeks with no email
blockers.cause: Google review backlog (reported in 2026 community threads).
blockers.fix: Check that the project's contact emails are monitored and correct, and follow up in the Verification Center or Google developer forums.

blockers.symptom: Verification needs a CASA security assessment
blockers.cause: The app requests a restricted scope (e.g. https://mail.google.com/) and stores or transmits the data on servers.
blockers.fix: Switch to sensitive scopes such as gmail.send if they're enough. Otherwise, budget for an assessment by an approved assessor.

blockers.symptom: Rate-limit or sending-limit errors at runtime
blockers.cause: Per-user quota units and daily sending caps (third-party reports: 6,000 units/min per user; 500 emails/day for personal accounts).
blockers.fix: Throttle and batch requests. These are runtime limits, not caps on how many users can connect.

composio.note: Composio's managed Gmail OAuth is the fastest way to prototype. Register your own Google Cloud OAuth client when you want your own branding on the consent screen, your own 100-user unverified cap and your own verification record. Composio's default scopes include https://mail.google.com/, which is restricted. On your own client that means several weeks of verification plus a yearly CASA assessment. If you can narrow to gmail.send or other sensitive scopes, verification is much lighter. We could not confirm whether Composio's managed client is already verified.

open_questions: We couldn't confirm whether Composio's managed Gmail client is already verified for the restricted https://mail.google.com/ scope.
Real review times are unclear. Google says 3-5 business days for sensitive scopes and 'several weeks' for restricted ones, but 2026 forum posts report waits of a month or more with no contact.
The exact console menu names for the consent screen and test-user list, and any official cap on the number of test users, weren't confirmed from official pages in this research.

We couldn't fetch Google's verification-requirements page (support.google.com/cloud/answer/13464321) or its annual reverification page (support.google.com/cloud/answer/13463816), so their details are unverified.
Logo rules, what the demo video must show, and the actual CASA cost for your app are not officially confirmed.
We didn't check the verification tier of the People API scopes in Composio's defaults (contacts.readonly, user.*.read).
We found no separate marketplace or listing review for a Gmail API OAuth client; Workspace Marketplace listing review was not researched.
